title: Grantham Institute Annual Lecture 2026 with Anne Hidalgo
desc:
Progress in the face of pushback

​Around the world, the leaders driving the most ambitious climate action are increasingly finding themselves at the centre of political polarisation, misinformation campaigns, and public backlash. Yet history shows that transformative change has rarely been achieved by following the path of least resistance. From redesigning cities and defending climate science to challenging vested interests, bold leadership often demands the willingness to go against the grain and withstand intense scrutiny.

title: Leadership in the Age of AI
desc:
The corporate world faces a growing engagement crisis. Around 80 percent of the global workforce is disengaged, depriving organisations of the passion, energy and commitment needed to unlock their full potential. title: Control and Optimisation seminar – Lei Zhang (Birmingham)
desc:
Title

Dimensions of Social Learning in Mind, Brain, and Machine

Abstract

Social learning, how we acquire knowledge from, for, and about others, emerges from multiple interacting dimensions: whom we interact with, how we draw inferences, and how we make decisions. This talk outlines a series of studies connecting these dimensions across cognitive, neural, and computational levels. I will present evidence that humans do not simply copy others but integrate actions and outcomes through structured and value-based inference. Neuroimaging findings show that social prediction and vicarious value rely on both domain-general learning mechanisms and socially specific neural computations. I will also discuss how social learning may go awry in individuals with mental health risks. Finally, I will…

title: Junior Analysis Seminar – Matteo Giardi (Max Planck)
desc:
Title

Abstract

We discuss local well-posedness in $H^s$ of solutions for the ideal incompressible magnetohydrodynamics system posed on $[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^d$. Building on a recent result, we show how the wave-null structure induced by a non-vanishing (constant) initial magnetic field can be leveraged to improve the classical Lisphitz threshold $s>d/2+1$ to $s>(d+1)/2$ for the velocity initial data.

Please note that the seminar will take place in person in room 140 of Huxley Building .

Click here to get to the Junior Analysis Seminar webpage .

title: SPC Seminar – Space – Dr. Dikshita Meggi (Leicester)
desc:
Speaker: Dr. Dikshita Meggi (Leicester)

Title: Martian ionospheric dynamics and the role of crustal magnetic fields

Abstract: Mars, without a global dipole magnetic field, has its atmosphere directly exposed to the solar wind. Their interactions with remnant crustal magnetic fields of varying strength and inclination, mainly in the southern hemisphere, further complicate ionospheric dynamics. We exploit observations from the Mars Advanced Radar for Subsurface and Ionosphere Sounding (MARSIS) on Mars Express. Using selected orbits over strong crustal fields and unmagnetised regions spanning 12 years, two-dimensional maps of ionospheric variability quantifying electron density deviations from Chapman-layer behaviour are constructed.

desc:
14:00 – 15:00 – Martin Wainwright (MIT)

Title: The Information Geometry of Diffusion Sampling

Abstract: Sampling from a high-dimensional distribution is a core challenge spanning statistics, operations research, applied mathematics and computer science. Diffusion-based methods have led to dramatic advances: in generative AI, they produce strikingly realistic images, video, and text, and they are finding growing use in areas including biology, drug design, materials science, and robotics. In this talk, we introduce a unified way of analyzing the performance of both continuous diffusion samplers (based on Gaussian noise), and discrete analogues. title: Jump Jet Book Launch
desc:
This is the story of how one man flew free of digital limits.

For an aircraft designer, taking your own concept from an idea to widespread, global operations is a rare achievement. Jump Jet tells the story of how Ralph Hooper did it with the Harrier, by side-stepping the emerging digital world.

With the creation of jet aircraft, nuclear weapons, and digital computers in the 1940s, the design of fighter aircraft was transformed. The analytical approach to design, where optimization ruled, was created. The only problem was that, for one key type of aircraft, it did not work.

Vertical take-off and landing aircraft, jump jets, were seen as essential to survive the opening salvoes of World War Three. Despite the need for them, almost every concept or prototype tried around the world…

title: Mind the Gap: Topological Quantum Blind Spots
desc:
Speaker: Dr Henry Legg (St Andrews)

Abstract:

Recently, significant attention has been focused on realising a topological qubit based on Majorana zero modes, driven in particular by claims from Microsoft Quantum. Here, I critically examine the Topological Gap Protocol (TGP) and demonstrate its fundamental Blind Spots. I show that the TGP is unreliable both as a diagnostic tool for topological superconductivity and associated Majorana zero modes, and as a method for verifying a bulk superconducting gap — a prerequisite for parity readout and qubit operation. Based on these insights, I will conclude that claims to have already realised topological qubits are not reliable and should be revisited.
